project_settings.approveModeAutopilotHint: Profiles set to Autopilot approve their own requests · only you can choose it
project_settings.approveModeDangerousHint: Every tool request of every agent in this project is approved at once: no review, no hold, nobody asked · only you can choose it
project_settings.approveModeDetail: Manual: every agent here runs as Manual — its allowed commands run, the reviewer judges the rest, then you. Autopilot: agents whose profile is set to Autopilot approve their own requests; work outside the worktree, pushes to a remote and other branches still ask you. Dangerous auto-approve: every tool request of every agent is approved at once, with no allowed list, hold, reviewer or question; questions and plans still come to you. Only you move it up; anyone, automation included, moves it down. A run can switch itself to Manual, never back. Kept on this computer only.
project_settings.dangerousFoot: The hold rules, the reviewer and the approved rules are not used while Dangerous auto-approve is chosen.

dangerousDialog.title: Turn on Dangerous auto-approve mode?
dangerousDialog.text: Every tool request of every agent in {{project}} will be approved at once. Nothing is reviewed or held and nobody is asked: not you, not the reviewer, not the Orchestrator. An agent, or text it read somewhere, can then:
dangerousDialog.push: Push or force-push to any branch
dangerousDialog.delete: Delete or overwrite files outside its worktree
dangerousDialog.credentials: Read credentials and send them out
dangerousDialog.run: Run any command, MCP tool or web page
dangerousDialog.after: It stays on until you turn it off here. What it approved is listed in each run's Conversation as “Approved by Dangerous auto-approve mode”.
dangerousDialog.confirm: Turn it on, I accept the risk

estimates.title: Estimates
estimates.label: Let Orchester estimate story points
estimates.hint: For tasks that have none, with a reason · uses the reviewer’s model and counts toward the daily budget
estimates.info: Orchester sizes each new task, and a task whose brief or criteria change, in story points (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 or 21) with a short reason, from the brief, the criteria and the project's merged tasks. Each estimate asks the reviewer’s model under Approvals and spends tokens, which count toward the project's daily budget. Points you set are never changed. Only you can change this, here in the window.
estimates.decisionHint: For tasks that have none · on {{connection}}, as the reviewer writes no reasons
estimates.decisionInfo: Estimates use {{connection}} · {{model}}, the project's default language reviewer, because a decision model writes no reasons. Each estimate spends tokens that count toward the daily budget. Points you set are never changed. Only you can change this setting, here in the window.
estimates.noLanguage: Estimates unavailable · no language reviewer is available in this project. Add a Claude Code connection to estimate story points with a reason.
estimates.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

orchestrator.onlyYou: Only you, here in the window
orchestrator.foot: Off: the Orchestrator proposes each change in the chat and you apply it, and no turn starts by itself. Each project has its own; a new project starts with it off.
orchestrator.blocked: A change brought by automation was not taken: only you change this setting, here in the window.

drive.label: Let the Orchestrator drive
drive.hint: It acts itself with Orchester's tools: runs, merges, answers, publishes, git
drive.info: Lets the Orchestrator's chat do in this project everything an outside agent can do through Orchester's MCP tools, without your click: start, cancel, pause and continue runs (accepting a step, raising limits and budgets and resuming after the daily budget included), merge runs (a finished run on its own too, unless its task says Don't merge automatically), answer agents and send them messages, publish the drafts it saves and write with git (what can lose work still waits for you). It starts a turn by itself for every wait of an agent and every run that stops, ends or succeeds, runs it started included. Each tool keeps its own rules and refusals: what widens what agents may do still needs Let automation change agent permissions. Off: it proposes each change in the chat and you apply it, and no turn starts by itself.
drive.on: The chat acts without asking in this project and keeps each change as an action in its conversation.
